# Make a factory improve itself

Source: https://github.com/fishuke/klin/blob/main/docs/site/guides/make-a-factory-improve-itself.md

This guide sets up the full improvement loop for a factory: scorers flag failures, Kiln proposes a definition change, replays prove it, a person reviews it, and a canary confirms it.

## Before you start

- The factory's definition lives in a [config repo](../configuration/definitions-as-code.md#config-repos-on-github), so proposals arrive as pull requests.
- The factory has done some real work, so there are runs to score.

## 1. Decide what "good" means

Write a scorer for the agent you want to improve. Make the labels concrete, and describe each one so the judge and your reviewers read them the same way.

```markdown
---
name: criteria
description: Does the change meet every acceptance criterion?
agents: [implement]
labels:
  - { value: meets, score: 1, description: Every criterion has a passing test }
  - { value: partly, score: 0.5, description: Some criteria have no test }
  - { value: misses, score: 0, description: The change does not do what was asked }
passingScore: 1
samplingRate: 25
model: claude-haiku-5-5
selfImprovement: true
---
Compare the acceptance criteria with the tests the run added or changed.
```

Save it as `scorers/criteria/scorer.md`. With `passingScore: 1`, only `meets` passes. See [Scorers](../measure-and-improve/scorers.md).

## 2. Set the thresholds

```yaml
# factory.yaml
selfImprovement:
  failedRunThreshold: 10
  maxAgeDays: 7
```

The check starts a proposal for an agent once its unreviewed failures cover 10 distinct runs, or the oldest is 7 days old. The default threshold is 25. A lower number gives you proposals sooner, with less evidence in each.

## 3. Put up guard rails

```yaml
# policies/guard.yaml
description: Self-improvement may tune agents, not the rules that check them
protectedPaths: [policies/**, gates/**, decisions/**, scorers/**]
twoApprovalPaths: [agents/review/**]
```

- Changes to `protectedPaths` are dropped from proposals. Kiln always drops `policies/` and `gates/`.
- Changes to `twoApprovalPaths` need two different people to approve.
- Protecting `scorers/**` stops the factory from making its own grading easier.

See [Policies and budgets](../configuration/policies-and-budgets.md).

## 4. Validate and merge

Open a pull request in the config repo with the three changes. The [validation workflow](../configuration/definitions-as-code.md#validate-pull-requests-with-github-actions) runs `kiln validate`. Merge it; the push applies the definition.

## 5. Let failures build up

Work as usual. About a quarter of the `implement` runs get a score. Check the agent's pass rate on the [dashboard](../measure-and-improve/metrics.md).

To try the loop without waiting, use **Run now** for the factory's self-improvement. It starts a proposal for every agent with at least one unreviewed failure.

## 6. Review the proposal

Kiln opens a pull request titled "Self-improvement: implement (instructions)" or similar. Read it in this order:

1. **Regressions addressed.** Each failed run, with its score and the judge's rationale. Do the failures look real?
2. **Replay.** The pass rate before and after, and a pass or fail per replayed run. A proposal that does not improve the after rate is a warning sign.
3. **Changes.** The changed files. By default, a "Lessons from reviewed failures" section in the agent's instructions.
4. **Dropped changes.** Any changes to protected paths that Kiln removed.

Then either:

- **Merge it.** If you merge it unchanged, the push applies it as a 10% canary and marks the proposal merged. If you edited the branch first, the push applies it to all new work items.
- **Approve it in Kiln instead.** Kiln applies it as a 10% canary without merging. This needs `definitions:write` on the factory. The pull request stays open; merging it later applies the change to everyone.
- **Reject it, with a reason.** The improver will not repeat a rejected lesson.

## 7. Watch the canary

Compare the candidate with the applied definition in the per-definition metrics. After 7 days, Kiln promotes the candidate if its pass rate is within 2 points of the applied one, and rolls it back otherwise. You can promote or roll back sooner. See [Replay and canary](../measure-and-improve/replay-and-canary.md).

## 8. Keep the loop honest

- Read a sample of passing runs now and then, to catch a judge that is too lenient.
- When a scorer's labels change, expect a wave of new failures. Raise `failedRunThreshold` for a while if needed.
- Benchmark before and after big changes to models or skills. See [Benchmarks](../measure-and-improve/benchmarks.md).

## Related pages

- [Self-improvement](../measure-and-improve/self-improvement.md)
- [Scorers](../measure-and-improve/scorers.md)
- [Replay and canary](../measure-and-improve/replay-and-canary.md)
- [Kiln builds Kiln](kiln-builds-kiln.md)

---

# Architecture and security

Source: https://github.com/fishuke/klin/blob/main/docs/site/infrastructure/architecture-and-security.md

Kiln is a control plane that receives events, decides what to do, and launches agents in disposable sandboxes; agents never run inside the control plane, and no agent identity can merge.

## Services

| Service | Responsibility |
| --- | --- |
| `api` | REST API under `/api/v1`, webhook endpoints, token auth and scopes, work items, gates, projects, definition apply |
| `orchestrator` | Drives work items through stages, gates, retries, budgets, the self-improvement schedule and benchmarks |
| `runner` | Launches sandboxes, issues run tokens, streams run events, collects artifacts |
| `integrations` | Adapters for GitHub, Linear, Jira and Slack; posts results back to the source |
| `mcp` | The Kiln MCP server, over streamable HTTP, with scoped tokens |
| `web` | Dashboard, inbox, product-owner workspace, definition viewer, portfolio |
| `scorer` | Runs judges on sampled runs, writes scores, groups failures |

Every external system sits behind an interface with a fake for tests: forge, tracker, chat, preview provider, sandbox provider, harness and decision provider.

## Where data lives

- **Definitions live in Git** or in Kiln's definition store, keyed by definition SHA. Runtime state never goes into the definition tree.
- **Runtime state** (work items, runs, run events, gates, scores, proposals, decision logs, audit entries, secrets, tokens) lives in Kiln's database.
- **Artifacts** (Playwright videos and reports, sandbox snapshots) go to object storage.
- **Events** go through an event bus with an outbox, so integrations, the scorer and the web app see them in order.

## How a run is isolated

1. Kiln issues a run token for the run's repositories.
2. The runner creates a sandbox from the agent's runner file: image, CPU and memory, setup commands and egress allowlist. See [Sandboxes](sandboxes.md).
3. Kiln clones the repositories with the run token and checks out the work item's `kiln/*` branch.
4. The harness starts inside the sandbox with the instructions, skills and a Kiln MCP connection that uses the same run token.
5. When the run ends, Kiln reads `.kiln/result.json`. If the run succeeded and the stage changes code, Kiln commits leftovers and pushes the branch with the run token. Then it destroys the sandbox. A paused run keeps a snapshot instead.

## Security controls

### No agent can merge

- A run token can push only `kiln/*` branches, open pull requests, comment and add labels, on the repositories of its run. It cannot approve or merge, and it expires after 60 minutes.
- Kiln checks the token before it pushes. A refused push fails the run.
- Agents are told not to push, open pull requests or merge. Kiln does those steps.
- Branch protection on your forge is the final control: require reviews on `main`, and do not give Kiln's GitHub identity a bypass.
- A work item cannot reach `complete` without a merge event or a person's confirmation. This rule is enforced in the state machine and covered by a property test.

### Commands are checked

The [command guard](../configuration/decisions.md#command-guard) rates shell commands before they run and blocks destructive ones or asks a person about risky ones. Claude Code checks every Bash call through a hook. Codex and OpenCode rely on the sandbox for isolation.

### Network is closed by default

Traffic from a sandbox goes through Kiln's egress proxy, which allows only the hosts of the run's repositories and the runner's `egress` list. Everything else is unreachable. On Kubernetes, a NetworkPolicy allows only DNS and the proxy.

### Sandboxes are locked down

Docker sandboxes drop all capabilities and set `no-new-privileges`. Kubernetes sandboxes run under gVisor (`runtimeClassName: gvisor`) as user 1000 (non-root), with no service account token mounted, privilege escalation off, all capabilities dropped and the default seccomp profile.

### Tokens are scoped per factory

API and MCP tokens carry scopes such as `read`, `send`, `decide:spec`, `decide:preview` and `definitions:write`, each for one factory or `*`. A product owner's token can approve previews without touching definitions. Tokens are stored as hashes. See [Admin, RBAC and audit](../management/admin-rbac-audit.md).

### Webhooks are verified

GitHub, Slack and Linear webhooks are checked against their signing secrets, Slack requests older than five minutes are refused, and Jira calls must carry the configured token. Custom webhooks use a bearer token, a URL token or a signature. Repeated deliveries are ignored.

### The factory cannot weaken its own checks

Self-improvement cannot change `policies/` or `gates/`, drops changes to any `protectedPaths`, needs two people for `twoApprovalPaths`, and never opens a proposal without a replay report. Agents cannot approve proposals. See [Policies and budgets](../configuration/policies-and-budgets.md).

### Content is not a source of permissions

Text in issues, tickets and Slack messages becomes the work item's request, never its permissions. What an agent may do comes from the definition, the run token and the gates. A reply in a thread or comment decides a gate only when its author is one of the gate's assignees, matched through the server's `identities` map.

### Everything is audited

Definition applies and rejections, gate decisions, steering, cancellations, pauses, proposals, canary changes, token issues and secret changes are written to the audit log with the actor.

## Design records

The decisions behind this architecture are written down as ADRs in `docs/adr/`:

- [0001 TypeScript monorepo](../../adr/0001-typescript-monorepo.md)
- [0002 Orchestration](../../adr/0002-orchestration.md)
- [0003 Definition format](../../adr/0003-definition-format.md)
- [0004 Harness adapters](../../adr/0004-harness-adapters.md)
- [0005 Storage](../../adr/0005-storage.md)
- [0006 Decision layer](../../adr/0006-decision-layer.md)
- [0007 Open source and bring your own keys](../../adr/0007-open-source-byok.md)
- [0008 Humans merge](../../adr/0008-humans-merge.md)

The [threat model](../../security/threat-model.md) lists the threats these controls answer.

## Data sent to model providers

Harnesses send the prompt, instructions, skills and the code they read to the model they use. Typed decisions send only the fields listed in each decision's `state`. Route model traffic through your own gateway if you need EU endpoints or zero data retention.

## Related pages

- [Sandboxes](sandboxes.md)
- [Harnesses](harnesses.md)
- [Self-hosting](self-hosting.md)
- [Typed decisions](../configuration/decisions.md)
- [Admin, RBAC and audit](../management/admin-rbac-audit.md)
- [Threat model](../../security/threat-model.md)
- [Architecture decision records](../../adr/README.md)

# Harnesses

Source: https://github.com/fishuke/klin/blob/main/docs/site/infrastructure/harnesses.md

A harness is the coding agent program that does the work in a run; Kiln supports Claude Code, Codex and OpenCode behind one adapter interface and does not write its own agent loop.

## Choosing a harness

Set `harness.type` in `agentDefaults`, on an agent or on an automation:

```yaml
harness: { type: claude-code, model: claude-sonnet-5-5 }
```

| `type` | Program | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `claude-code` | `claude` | The default when nothing sets a harness. |
| `codex` | `codex` | |
| `opencode` | `opencode` | The `oz` harness type becomes `opencode` on import. |

The harness program must be installed in the runner's image. Pin its version in the image, because flags and output formats change between releases.

## How each harness runs

| | Claude Code | Codex | OpenCode |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Command | `claude -p --output-format stream-json --input-format stream-json --verbose --permission-mode bypassPermissions --append-system-prompt <instructions>` | `codex exec --json --skip-git-repo-check --dangerously-bypass-approvals-and-sandbox <instructions + prompt>` | `opencode run --format json <prompt>` |
| Model flag | `--model` | `-m` | `-m` |
| Instructions | Appended to the system prompt | Sent before the prompt | Written to `AGENTS.md` |
| Skills folder | `.claude/skills/` | `.agents/skills/` | `.opencode/skills/` |
| Kiln MCP | Written to `.mcp.json` | Not configured | Not configured |
| Command guard | `PreToolUse` hook on Bash in `.claude/settings.json` | Not installed | Not installed |
| Cost | Reported by Claude Code | Estimated from token counts | Reported per step |

## Credentials

Kiln passes model credentials to the harness as environment variables of the run, read from Kiln's secrets. You bring your own keys. Set them with `harness.auth`:

```yaml
harness:
  type: claude-code
  auth: { source: secret, secretName: CLAUDE_TOKEN }
```

| `auth` | What the run gets |
| --- | --- |
| `{ source: secret, secretName: <name> }` | A typed secret (such as `claude_oauth_token` or `anthropic_bedrock_access_key`) gives its provider variables. Otherwise, the secret's value. For Claude Code it is set as `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` when it is a subscription token from `claude setup-token` (it starts with `sk-ant-oat`), and as `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` otherwise. For Codex it is `OPENAI_API_KEY`. For OpenCode the variable has the secret's name. Add `env: <VARIABLE>` to choose the variable yourself. A missing secret fails the run. |
| `{ source: worker }` | No credential from Kiln. The harness uses credentials already present on the worker or in the image. |
| not set | Kiln looks for default secrets, including typed team and personal secrets and the team-managed model keys. Claude Code gets the first of `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN`, `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` and Bedrock credentials that is set. Codex gets the first of `OPENAI_API_KEY` and `CODEX_API_KEY`. OpenCode gets every one of `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, `OPENAI_API_KEY`, `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` and `GOOGLE_GENERATIVE_AI_API_KEY` that is set. |

The agent's `secrets` list is passed the same way, one variable per secret. Credentials go only to that run's sandbox, and personal secrets only to runs their owner triggered. Secret values are redacted from run output. See [Secrets, MCP servers and environments](../management/secrets-mcps-environments.md).

## Isolation

The sandbox is the security boundary for all three. Permission prompts are off because nobody is there to answer them; the [command guard](../configuration/decisions.md#command-guard) and the sandbox take their place.

## What a run receives

- **Instructions:** the agent's Markdown body, matching factory memories, any extra instructions, and a "Reporting back to Kiln" section.
- **Prompt:** the work item's title, body, triage result, acceptance criteria, review findings and messages from people, plus a line telling the agent what this stage needs.
- **Skills:** every shared skill plus the agent's own.
- **Environment:** `KILN_RUN_ID`, `KILN_RUN_TOKEN`, `KILN_FACTORY`, `KILN_AGENT_TYPE`, `KILN_WORK_ITEM` and `KILN_STAGE`.
- **Working directory:** the first repository, checked out on the work item's `kiln/*` branch. All non-deferred repositories are cloned side by side.

## The result file

Agents report structured results by writing `.kiln/result.json` in the repository root. Kiln excludes `.kiln/` from git, so the file is never committed. Kiln reads it after the run; if the JSON does not parse, the run records an error event.

| `agentType` | Shape |
| --- | --- |
| `TRIAGE` | `{"kind": "feature\|bug\|chore\|incident\|question", "size": "xs\|s\|m\|l\|xl", "summary": "...", "duplicateOf": "optional issue key"}` |
| `FOREMAN` | `{"dispatch": {"stage": "triage\|spec\|build\|review\|handoff", "agent": "name", "context": "..."}}` or `{"ask": "question for the requester"}` |
| `SPEC` | `{"specPath": "docs/specs/<id>.md", "criteria": ["AC1: ..."], "stories": ["..."], "openQuestions": ["..."]}` |
| `IMPLEMENT` | `{"summary": "...", "testsPassed": true, "memories": [{"title": "...", "body": "..."}]}` |
| `VERIFY` | `{"testsPassed": true, "playwrightReport": "playwright-report/results.json"}` |
| `REVIEW` | `{"verdict": "accepted\|changes_requested\|needs_human", "findings": ["file:line — issue — fix"]}` |
| `PLAN` | `{"epics": [{"title": "...", "milestone": "...", "dependsOn": [], "issues": [{"title": "...", "body": "...", "criteria": ["..."], "factory": "alias"}]}]}` |
| Others | `{"summary": "..."}` |

What Kiln does with it:

- A review verdict of `changes_requested` with findings loops back to build. `needs_human` posts the findings on the pull request for a person.
- A spec without `specPath` is recorded as `docs/specs/<work item id>.md`.
- `memories` from any agent become memory proposals.
- `testsPassed` is checked when a pipeline stage requires `tests_pass`.

The agent commits on the current branch. It must not push, open pull requests or merge; Kiln does that with a scoped token.

## Run events

Kiln streams each harness's output as normalized events: `message`, `tool_call`, `tool_result`, `steer`, `error`, plus Kiln's own `started`, `guard`, `pushed`, `resumed` and `finished`. Events are stored in order, can be read after the fact, and can be followed live over server-sent events.

## Steering

Steering sends a message to a running agent.

| Harness | How the message arrives |
| --- | --- |
| Claude Code | Written to the session's input as a new user message, so the agent reads it before its next step. |
| Codex | Queued. When the current turn ends, Kiln resumes the session (`codex exec resume --last`) with the message. |
| OpenCode | Queued. When the current turn ends, Kiln continues the session (`opencode run --continue`) with the message. |

You can steer from the run page, the API, the Kiln MCP, or by replying where the work started: a Slack thread, a Linear or Jira issue, or a GitHub issue or pull request. A reply steers the running agent when it does not decide a gate or answer an open question. When no agent is running, the reply is added to the conversation instead, and the next agent run sees it under "Messages from people".

Each steering message is kept on the run record, counted as a human touch on the work item, and written to the audit log. A resumed run gets the steering messages so far. Steering a run that has finished fails.

## Related pages

- [Factory agents](../configuration/agents.md)
- [Sandboxes](sandboxes.md)
- [Skills](../configuration/skills.md)
- [Replay and canary](../measure-and-improve/replay-and-canary.md)
- [API overview](../developer-tools/api.md)

# Sandboxes

Source: https://github.com/fishuke/klin/blob/main/docs/site/infrastructure/sandboxes.md

Every agent run gets a fresh sandbox built from its runner file, and Kiln destroys the sandbox when the run ends.

## Runner files

```yaml
# runners/linux-node.yaml
description: Node 22 with pnpm
image: node:22-bookworm
backend: docker
shape: { vcpus: 4, memoryGb: 8 }
setupCommands:
  - corepack enable
  - pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
egress:
  - github.com
  - registry.npmjs.org
```

| Key | Default | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `image` | required | The container image. Docker pulls it if it is not cached. |
| `backend` | `docker` | `docker`, `kubernetes` or `local`. |
| `shape` | none | `vcpus` and `memoryGb`. Sets CPU and memory limits. |
| `setupCommands` | `[]` | Run in order after the repositories are cloned. A failing command fails the run. |
| `egress` | `[]` | Extra host names the sandbox may reach, such as package registries and your model gateway. The hosts of the repositories it clones are always allowed. |
| `description` | none | |

An agent picks a runner with `runner: <name>`, usually inherited from `agentDefaults`. An agent without a runner uses `node:22-bookworm` on the server's default backend, which is `local` unless the server sets another.

## Backends

### Local

The workspace is a temporary directory on the Kiln host. It runs setup commands and the command guard, but it cannot enforce egress, CPU or memory limits. Use it for development and tests only.

### Docker

Each run is a container started with `sleep infinity` and `/workspace` as its working directory:

- labels `kiln.sandbox=1`, `kiln.dev/run` and `kiln.dev/factory`,
- `--cpus` and `--memory` from `shape`,
- `--security-opt no-new-privileges` and `--cap-drop ALL`,
- the `kiln-egress` network with `HTTPS_PROXY` and `HTTP_PROXY` set to `http://kiln-egress-proxy:3128` and `KILN_EGRESS_ALLOW` set to the allowed hosts: the runner's `egress` list plus the hosts of the cloned repositories. With no hosts at all, the container gets `--network none`.

### Kubernetes with gVisor

Each run is a pod in the `kiln-sandboxes` namespace, plus a NetworkPolicy for that pod:

- `runtimeClassName: gvisor`, so the pod runs in gVisor's user-space kernel,
- `runAsNonRoot` as user 1000, `RuntimeDefault` seccomp, no privilege escalation, all capabilities dropped,
- no service account token mounted, `restartPolicy: Never`,
- requests and limits from `shape`,
- an `emptyDir` volume at `/workspace`.

The NetworkPolicy blocks all ingress. When there are no allowed hosts at all, it blocks all egress too. Otherwise it allows only DNS (UDP 53 to `kube-dns`) and TCP 3128 to the pod labeled `app.kubernetes.io/name: kiln-egress-proxy`, which enforces the host list.

Kiln waits up to 120 seconds for the pod to be ready. Your cluster needs a `gvisor` RuntimeClass and the egress proxy deployed.

## Egress

Agents need the network to clone, install packages and call model APIs. Kiln keeps that surface small:

- The hosts of the repositories the run clones, such as `github.com`, are always allowed.
- List every other host the run needs in `egress`, such as `registry.npmjs.org`. Nothing else is reachable.
- The proxy enforces host names, so you do not have to track IP addresses.
- Keep model traffic going to your model gateway, and list only the gateway.

## What Kiln does in the sandbox

Kiln runs its own commands as trusted, so the command guard does not check them:

- configure git as `kiln-agent[bot]` and exclude `.kiln/` from git,
- check out the work item's branch, or the pinned commit for replays and benchmarks,
- write skills and harness settings,
- after the run, commit leftovers and push the branch with the run token.

Commands the agent runs through the sandbox's command API pass the [command guard](../configuration/decisions.md#command-guard).

## Pause and resume

A running agent can be paused, for example while it waits at a gate, and resumed later on any node.

- **Pause** packs `/workspace` into a `.tgz` archive, stores it in object storage under `snapshots/<sandbox>/<time>.tgz`, and stops the agent. The run's status becomes `paused` and the sandbox is kept until it resumes.
- **Resume** starts a new sandbox from the same runner, possibly on another node or backend, unpacks the snapshot into `/workspace`, and starts the harness again with the original request and any steering messages so far.
- The run records the workspace hash at pause and at resume, so you can check the workspace is the same.

Snapshots hold files only. On Docker, the server can also be set to take a CRIU checkpoint that keeps processes; the snapshot records whether it did. Kubernetes snapshots never keep processes.

## Related pages

- [Harnesses](harnesses.md)
- [Architecture and security](architecture-and-security.md)
- [Self-hosting](self-hosting.md)
- [Typed decisions](../configuration/decisions.md)

# Self-hosting

Source: https://github.com/fishuke/klin/blob/main/docs/site/infrastructure/self-hosting.md

Kiln runs on your own infrastructure: a single host with Docker for small installs, or a Kubernetes cluster with gVisor for production.

## Requirements

| Component | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| Node 22 and pnpm 10 | Kiln's services are TypeScript on Node. |
| A data directory (a volume) | Runtime state (work items, runs, gates, scores, tokens, audit log) in `kiln.json`, and objects (videos, reports, snapshots) under `objects/`. Back it up by copying it. |
| Docker, or Kubernetes with a `gvisor` RuntimeClass | Sandboxes for agent runs. Without either, runs use host directories (development only). |
| An egress proxy | Enforces each runner's `egress` host list. Included in `docker-compose.yml` and the Helm chart. See [Sandboxes](sandboxes.md#egress). |
| Optional: an OpenAI-compatible gateway (LiteLLM) | The LLM fallback for typed decisions and judges. |

Postgres, Temporal, NATS and S3 are not required in v1; see ADR-002 and ADR-005 for why and for the path to them.

## Install

### Try it locally

```bash
git clone https://github.com/fishuke/klin kiln && cd kiln
pnpm install
pnpm dev            # API on :4000 with demo data, web app on :3000
```

Open http://localhost:3000. Demo factories run on a git-backed local forge with scripted agents, so nothing needs an account.

### One machine with Docker Compose

```bash
cp .env.example .env          # add your keys: CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN from `claude setup-token`, or API keys
echo KILN_AGENTS=real >> .env  # run Claude Code, Codex and OpenCode instead of scripted agents
docker build -t kiln-runner-node runners/images/node
docker compose up -d --build
pnpm health
```

The API prints a bootstrap admin token on first start (also in the data volume as `admin-token`). Put it in `.env` as `KILN_TOKEN` so the web app can call the API, then restart `web`.

Then create your account: the first signup (`POST /api/v1/auth/signup`) becomes the owner of the default team, and existing factories move into that team. Invite everyone else. See [Teams and users](../management/teams-and-users.md).

### Kubernetes with Helm

```bash
kubectl create secret generic kiln-env --from-env-file=.env
helm install kiln deploy/helm/kiln \
  --set publicUrl=https://kiln.example.com --set webUrl=https://kiln.example.com \
  --set ingress.host=kiln.example.com
```

The chart creates the `kiln-sandboxes` namespace with the restricted pod security level, a `gvisor` RuntimeClass (handler `runsc`, which your nodes must provide), the egress proxy, a default-deny NetworkPolicy, and a Role that lets the API create sandbox pods there.

### First factory

```bash
pnpm kiln init my-factory --template sdlc
# edit my-factory/factory.yaml: repositories, alias, integrations
pnpm kiln validate my-factory
KILN_URL=http://localhost:4000 KILN_TOKEN=... pnpm kiln apply my-factory
pnpm kiln send "Fix the typo in the README" --factory <alias>
```

Or push the folder to a GitHub repo and connect it under Create factory; merges to its default branch then apply automatically.

## Connect your systems

### Public URLs

Kiln needs two URLs:

- **Public URL:** where agents in sandboxes reach the API. Kiln uses it for the Claude Code command-guard hook (`/api/v1/guard`) and the Kiln MCP (`/mcp`). Without it, neither is installed in runs.
- **Web URL:** where people open links. Kiln uses it in the links it posts, such as `<web URL>/inbox/<gate>` and `<web URL>/runs/<work item>`.

### Webhooks and secrets

Point each provider's webhooks at Kiln and set the matching secret. For the four provider endpoints, Kiln reads the server environment variable with the secret's name (for example `GITHUB_WEBHOOK_SECRET`) first, then its secrets store, then `KILN_SECRET_<NAME>`. A custom webhook's secret comes from the secrets store or `KILN_SECRET_<secretName>`.

| Provider | Endpoint | Secret |
| --- | --- | --- |
| GitHub | `POST /webhooks/github` | `GITHUB_WEBHOOK_SECRET` |
| Slack | `POST /webhooks/slack` | `SLACK_SIGNING_SECRET` |
| Linear | `POST /webhooks/linear` | `LINEAR_WEBHOOK_SECRET` |
| Jira | `POST /webhooks/jira?token=<token>` | `JIRA_WEBHOOK_TOKEN` |
| Custom | `POST /webhooks/<factory>/<name>` | The webhook file's `secretName` |

When a provider secret is not set, Kiln accepts that provider's webhooks without checking signatures. Set every secret before you expose Kiln to the internet.

Admins can set secrets through the API; values are never returned, only names. See the [API overview](../developer-tools/api.md).

### Model credentials

Runs use your own model keys. Store `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` (a Claude subscription token from `claude setup-token`) or `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` for Claude Code, `OPENAI_API_KEY` or `CODEX_API_KEY` for Codex, and the keys OpenCode's providers need. You can store them as Kiln secrets or set them as plain environment variables on the server. Agents can also name their own secret with `harness.auth`. See [Harnesses](harnesses.md#credentials).

### Accounts and login

| Variable | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `KILN_OPEN_SIGNUP=1` | Anyone may sign up and join the default team. Otherwise, after the first owner, signup needs an invite. |
| `GITHUB_CLIENT_ID`, `GITHUB_CLIENT_SECRET` | Turn on GitHub login. The OAuth app's callback URL is `<KILN_PUBLIC_URL>/api/v1/auth/github/callback`. `GITHUB_OAUTH_URL` and `GITHUB_API_URL` point at GitHub Enterprise. |
| `KILN_SECRET_KEY` | Seals team and personal secrets with AES-256-GCM, and signs run tokens. Set it, and keep it stable across restarts. |
| `KILN_DEV_AUTH=1` | Local development only: requests without a token act as `dev@kiln.local`, owner of the default team. |

### Identities

Gate assignees are people, such as `po@acme.test`. To let replies in Slack or on issues decide gates, people link their Slack, GitHub, Linear, Jira, Discord, Teams, GitLab or Azure DevOps accounts in user settings. See [Linked accounts](../management/teams-and-users.md#linked-accounts). The server option `identities` still works as a fallback. It is keyed by `<provider>:<user>`, for example `slack:U024BE7LH` → `po@acme.test`. See [Who may decide from a reply](../configuration/automations.md#who-may-decide-from-a-reply).

### Roles

Gates name approvers by role, such as `role:po` or `role:code-owners`. Kiln's server configuration maps each role to people. Kiln uses these roles:

| Role | Used by |
| --- | --- |
| `po` | Built-in spec and preview gates |
| `code-owners` | The built-in merge gate, and high-risk reviews |
| `admins` | Command approvals for runs without a requester |

### Sandboxes

- **Docker:** create the `kiln-egress` network and run the egress proxy on it as `kiln-egress-proxy`, listening on port 3128.
- **Kubernetes:** create the `kiln-sandboxes` namespace, install gVisor with a RuntimeClass named `gvisor`, and deploy the egress proxy with the label `app.kubernetes.io/name: kiln-egress-proxy` on port 3128.
- Build runner images with the harness programs (`claude`, `codex`, `opencode`), git and your toolchain installed.

### Forge identity

Kiln talks to GitHub with a token, for example a GitHub App installation token. It needs to read repositories, push `kiln/*` branches, open and update pull requests, comment, add labels and read check runs. Do not give it a branch-protection bypass. Agents never see this token; each run gets its own short-lived run token instead.

## Timers

Kiln runs a timer pass that:

- sends gate nudges and applies gate expiry,
- fires due schedules,
- retries verify stages that wait for CI,
- promotes or rolls back canaries after 7 days,
- when self-improvement checks are switched on for the pass, runs the check for every factory.

## Monitoring

- `GET /api/v1/health` returns `ok`, the number of factories and the server time.
- Each run records a trace ID, so you can match its events with your logs and traces.
- The audit log lists who applied definitions, decided gates, steered runs, issued tokens and set secrets.

## Troubleshooting

| Symptom | Check |
| --- | --- |
| A definition push did not apply | The factory's last error shows the first validation error. Run `kiln validate`. |
| An automation never fires | The trigger's `provider` and `event` match the event name exactly, and every filter key matches (GitHub events carry both `repo` and `repos`). |
| A work item is `blocked` | Its blocked reason says why: an expired gate, a stage that failed too often, the budget, or an error. Answer the open question to resume. |
| A run fails at install | The runner's `egress` list is missing a package registry or another host the run needs. Repository hosts are always allowed. |
| Verify waits forever | CI checks on the branch are still pending. Kiln checks again on each timer pass. |
| Every command is blocked | The Claude Code hook cannot reach the public URL, so it blocks by design. |
| Webhooks return 401 | The secret in Kiln does not match the provider's. |

- [Architecture and security](architecture-and-security.md)
- [Sandboxes](sandboxes.md)
- [Harnesses](harnesses.md)
- [GitHub](../integrations/github.md)
- [Admin, RBAC and audit](../management/admin-rbac-audit.md)

# GitHub

Source: https://github.com/fishuke/klin/blob/main/docs/site/integrations/github.md

GitHub is both a source of work and the place where Kiln delivers it: issues and comments start work items, Kiln opens pull requests on `kiln/*` branches, and a person's merge completes the work.

## Set up

1. Give Kiln a GitHub token, for example from a GitHub App, that can read the factory's repositories, push branches, open and update pull requests, comment, add labels and read check runs. See [Self-hosting](../infrastructure/self-hosting.md#forge-identity).
2. Add a webhook to each repository (or the organization) pointing at `POST /webhooks/github`, with content type `application/json` and a secret. Store the secret in Kiln as `GITHUB_WEBHOOK_SECRET`.
3. Send these events: Issues, Issue comments, Pull requests, Pull request reviews, Check suites and Pushes.
4. List the repositories in `factory.yaml` under `repositories`.
5. Protect `main`: require reviews and status checks, and do not let Kiln's identity bypass them.

Kiln verifies `X-Hub-Signature-256` on every call and ignores repeated `X-GitHub-Delivery` IDs.

## Starting work

Add an automation for the events you want. A common one:

```markdown
---
triggers:
  - provider: github
    event: issue_labeled
    filter:
      repo: [acme/web]
      labels: [kiln-ready]
---
Take the labeled issue through the factory.
```

| Event | Fires when |
| --- | --- |
| `issue_opened` | An issue is opened. `mentioned` holds the `@handles` in its body. |
| `issue_labeled` | A label is added. `label` is the new label; `labels` is all labels. |
| `issue_assigned` | Someone is assigned. |
| `issue_mentioned` | A comment is added to an issue. |
| `pull_request_mentioned` | A comment is added to a pull request. |
| `pull_request_opened`, `pull_request_labeled` | A pull request is opened or labeled. |
| `pull_request_review_submitted` | A review is submitted. |
| `pull_request_merged`, `pull_request_closed` | A pull request is merged, or closed without merging. |
| `check_suite_completed` | A check suite finishes. |
| `push` | A branch is pushed. `head` is the branch name. |

A comment that mentions the factory's alias, such as `@webapp please take this`, starts foreman work in a factory with no automations. See [Automations](../configuration/automations.md).

## What Kiln does on GitHub

- **Branches.** Each work item gets one branch, `kiln/<id>-<title-slug>`. Kiln pushes it with the run's token, which can push only `kiln/*` branches.
- **Spec pull request.** When the work needs a spec, Kiln opens a draft pull request with the spec and the acceptance criteria as a checklist.
- **Pull request body.** It links the work item, the source and the tracker issue, lists the acceptance criteria, and ends with "Opened by the Kiln factory `<alias>`. A person reviews and merges."
- **CI.** The verify stage waits for check runs on the branch. Failures, cancellations and timeouts loop the work back to build.
- **Preview card.** With a preview provider, Kiln comments a card with the preview URL, test counts and one video link per acceptance criterion.
- **Review findings.** Findings that need a person's judgment are posted as a comment.
- **Ready for review.** When the build stage succeeds, Kiln opens the pull request, or takes the spec pull request out of draft.
- **Hand-off.** Kiln adds the label `factory:<alias>` and posts "Ready to merge" with the pull request link where the work started, for example on the source issue.

## After hand-off

- **Merge.** When a person merges the pull request, the `pull_request` webhook completes the work item and closes its open gates.
- **Review comments.** A submitted review that is not an approval sends the work item back to build, with the review text as findings.
- **Comments.** Comments on the source issue or the pull request decide an open spec or preview gate, answer an open question, steer a running agent, or are added to the work item's conversation. Map GitHub logins to people with the server's `identities` option (`github:<login>`). Replies decide a gate only when their author is one of its assignees; see [Who may decide from a reply](../configuration/automations.md#who-may-decide-from-a-reply).

## Config repos

A factory's definition can live in a GitHub repository. Merges to its branch apply the new definition when Kiln receives the `push` webhook, so install the webhook on the config repo too. See [Definitions as code](../configuration/definitions-as-code.md#config-repos-on-github).

## Related pages

- [Automations](../configuration/automations.md)
- [How Kiln works](../overview/how-kiln-works.md)
- [Previews](previews.md)
- [Definitions as code](../configuration/definitions-as-code.md)
- [Architecture and security](../infrastructure/architecture-and-security.md)

# Jira

Source: https://github.com/fishuke/klin/blob/main/docs/site/integrations/jira.md

Jira works like Linear in Kiln: issues and comments start or continue work items, updates go back as comments, and the planning agent can create its roadmap in a Jira project.

## Set up

1. Create a Jira API token for a service account. Give Kiln the site URL, the account's email, the token and the project key. Kiln calls Jira's REST API v3 with basic auth.
2. Add a Jira webhook pointing at `POST /webhooks/jira?token=<token>` for issue created, issue updated and comment created events.
3. Store the same token in Kiln as `JIRA_WEBHOOK_TOKEN`. Once it is set, Kiln refuses calls that do not carry it. Kiln also ignores repeated `X-Atlassian-Webhook-Identifier` values.
4. Add `jira` to the factory's `integrations`.

## Starting work

| Event | Fires when |
| --- | --- |
| `issue_created` | An issue is created. |
| `issue_assigned` | An issue is updated and its assignee changed. Other updates are ignored. |
| `issue_mentioned` | A comment is added. `mentioned` holds the `@handles` in it. |

Filter on `project`, `labels`, `mentioned` or `assignee`:

```markdown
---
agent: foreman
triggers:
  - provider: jira
    event: issue_created
    filter:
      project: [KIL]
      labels: [kiln]
---
```

The issue key, such as `KIL-42`, links the work item to the issue.

## What Kiln does in Jira

- **Updates.** Gate requests, reminders, "Ready to merge" and "Done" are posted as comments.
- **Replies.** Comments on the issue continue the work item. They decide an open spec or preview gate, answer an open question, steer a running agent, or are added to the conversation. Map Jira users to people with the server's `identities` option (`jira:<user>`). Replies decide a gate only when their author is one of its assignees; see [Who may decide from a reply](../configuration/automations.md#who-may-decide-from-a-reply).
- **States.** At hand-off, Kiln moves the issue through the first transition into the "In Progress" status category. On completion, it uses the first transition into the "Done" category.
- **Duplicates.** Triage reads the project's 20 most recently created issues to spot duplicates.
- **Text.** Kiln writes descriptions and comments in Atlassian Document Format, one paragraph per blank-line-separated block.

## Planning

The [planning agent](../product-owners/planning.md) can create its roadmap in the Jira project: a Task per epic, labeled `epic`, with a Sub-task for each piece of work. Each sub-task has an acceptance criteria checklist and a `factory:<alias>` label.

## Related pages

- [Automations](../configuration/automations.md)
- [Linear](linear.md)
- [Planning](../product-owners/planning.md)
- [How Kiln works](../overview/how-kiln-works.md)

---

# Linear

Source: https://github.com/fishuke/klin/blob/main/docs/site/integrations/linear.md

Linear can start work items, receives the factory's updates as comments on the issue, and is where the planning agent creates roadmap issues.

## Set up

1. Create a Linear API key and note the ID of the team the factory works with. Kiln uses the key for comments, state changes, recent issues and new issues.
2. Add a webhook in Linear pointing at `POST /webhooks/linear` for Issue and Comment events, and for agent session events if you use Linear's agent features.
3. Store the webhook's signing secret in Kiln as `LINEAR_WEBHOOK_SECRET`. Kiln checks the `Linear-Signature` header and ignores repeated `Linear-Delivery` IDs.
4. Add `linear` to the factory's `integrations`.

## Starting work

| Event | Fires when |
| --- | --- |
| `issue_created` | An issue is created. |
| `issue_assigned` | An issue's assignee changes. |
| `issue_mentioned` | A comment is added. `mentioned` holds the `@handles` in it. |
| `agent_session_created` | Someone starts an agent session on an issue, for example by assigning or mentioning the factory's agent. |

Filter on `team_ids`, `labels`, `mentioned` or `assignee`:

```markdown
---
triggers:
  - provider: linear
    event: agent_session_created
    filter: { team_ids: [391c8fd6-4bb1-4493-ae5d-02b01ce045e2] }
---
```

A comment that mentions the factory's alias starts foreman work in a factory with no automations.

## What Kiln does in Linear

- **Updates.** Gate requests, reminders, "Ready to merge" and "Done" are posted as comments on the issue.
- **Replies.** Comments on the issue continue the work item. A comment starting with `approve` or `reject` decides an open spec or preview gate, and other text answers an open question, steers a running agent, or is added to the conversation. Map Linear users to people with the server's `identities` option (`linear:<user>`). Replies decide a gate only when their author is one of its assignees; see [Who may decide from a reply](../configuration/automations.md#who-may-decide-from-a-reply).
- **States.** At hand-off, Kiln moves the issue to the team's first `started` state. When the work completes, it moves it to the first `completed` state.
- **Duplicates.** Triage reads the team's 20 most recent issues to spot duplicates.

## Planning

The [planning agent](../product-owners/planning.md) creates its roadmap in Linear: one issue per epic, with a sub-issue for each piece of work. The epic is labeled `epic`. Each sub-issue has an "Acceptance criteria" checklist, a `factory:<alias>` label and a "Factory: @<alias>" line. Kiln looks labels up by name and creates any that are missing on the team.

## Related pages

- [Automations](../configuration/automations.md)
- [Planning](../product-owners/planning.md)
- [Jira](jira.md)
- [How Kiln works](../overview/how-kiln-works.md)

# Previews

Source: https://github.com/fishuke/klin/blob/main/docs/site/integrations/previews.md

A preview provider deploys each factory pull request to its own URL, so a person can try the change and accept it before review and merge.

## How previews fit in

When a preview provider is configured, the foreman's default path adds a preview stage after verify. In a [pipeline](../configuration/pipelines-and-gates.md), add it yourself:

```yaml
- { id: preview, action: preview.deploy, gate: preview-acceptance }
```

The preview stage:

1. Deploys the work item's branch.
2. Comments a card on the pull request with the preview URL, the pull request link, the test counts and a table of acceptance criteria with their result and a video link.
3. Moves the work item to `awaiting_preview` and opens the stage's gate with the card, the preview URL and each video as evidence.

The stage is skipped when no provider is configured or the work item has no pull request. Without a `gate`, the stage deploys and moves on.

Approving the gate moves the work on. Rejecting it sends the work back to build with your feedback. When it comes back, Kiln deploys again and asks again. See [Approving specs and previews](../product-owners/approving-specs-and-previews.md).

## Providers

Kiln uses one preview provider per installation.

### Vercel

Kiln creates a preview deployment through Vercel's API from the GitHub branch. It needs:

| Setting | Notes |
| --- | --- |
| Token | A Vercel access token. |
| Project | The Vercel project name. |
| Team ID | Optional. For projects owned by a team. |

The preview URL is the deployment's URL.

### Kubernetes

Kiln applies one namespace per pull request with `kubectl apply`:

- a Namespace named `preview-<repo>-pr-<number>` (lowercased, at most 63 characters), labeled `kiln.dev/preview: "true"`,
- a Deployment `app` with one replica of your image,
- a Service `app` on port 80,
- an Ingress for the host `pr-<number>.<repo>.<domain>`.

| Setting | Notes |
| --- | --- |
| Domain | The base domain for preview hosts. Point a wildcard DNS record and certificate at your ingress controller. |
| Image | How to name the image for a repository and branch. Your CI must build and push that image. |
| Port | The container port. Default 3000. |

The preview URL is `https://pr-<number>.<repo>.<domain>`. Destroying a preview deletes its namespace.

## Evidence on the card

The card's criteria table comes from the verify stage. The verify agent runs Playwright with video on and writes a JSON report to `playwright-report/results.json`. Kiln matches tests to criteria by the `AC<number>` in each test title, such as `AC1: the settings page has a dark mode switch`, and uploads one video per criterion to object storage. See [Writing acceptance criteria](../product-owners/acceptance-criteria.md).

## Related pages

- [Approving specs and previews](../product-owners/approving-specs-and-previews.md)
- [Pipelines and gates](../configuration/pipelines-and-gates.md)
- [GitHub](github.md)
- [Self-hosting](../infrastructure/self-hosting.md)

# Slack

Source: https://github.com/fishuke/klin/blob/main/docs/site/integrations/slack.md

In Slack, you mention a factory's alias to start work, and the whole work item then lives in that thread: questions, approvals, the preview and the pull request link.

## Set up

1. Create a Slack app with a bot user and the `chat:write` scope. Give Kiln the bot token.
2. Turn on Event Subscriptions with the request URL `POST /webhooks/slack`. Kiln answers Slack's URL verification challenge.
3. Subscribe to the bot events `app_mention`, `message.channels`, `message.im` and `reaction_added`.
4. Store the app's signing secret in Kiln as `SLACK_SIGNING_SECRET`.
5. Add `slack` to the factory's `integrations` and invite the bot to the channels you use.

Kiln checks Slack's signature and refuses requests whose timestamp is more than five minutes old. It answers Slack right away and does the work in the background. Retries with the same `event_id` are ignored.

## Starting work

Mention the factory's alias:

```text
@webapp the footer link to /pricing is broken
```

The first line becomes the work item's title, and the rest becomes its body. A list of bulleted requirements in the body helps triage size the request.

A factory with no automations answers mentions of its alias. To control it, add an automation:

```markdown
---
triggers:
  - provider: slack
    event: app_mention
    filter: { channel: [C0123ABCD] }
---
```

Without a `mentioned` filter, an `app_mention` trigger fires only for the factory named in the message, or for every factory when the message only mentions the bot.

| Event | Fires when |
| --- | --- |
| `app_mention` | The bot is mentioned. |
| `direct_message` | Someone sends the bot a direct message. |
| `thread_reply` | Someone replies in a thread. |
| `reaction_added` | Someone adds a reaction. `reaction` holds its name. |

Messages from bots are ignored.

## Working in the thread

Kiln posts to the thread where the work started:

- questions and gate requests, such as "Approve the spec", with the details and a link to decide in the inbox,
- reminders when a gate waits past its nudge time,
- "Ready to merge" with the pull request and preview links,
- "Done" when the pull request is merged.

Reply in the thread to act on the work item:

| Reply starts with | Effect |
| --- | --- |
| `approve`, `approved`, `lgtm`, `ship it` or `accept` | Approves the open spec or preview gate. |
| `reject`, `changes:` or `request changes` | Rejects it. The rest of your message is the feedback. |
| Anything else | Answers an open question. If there is none and an agent is running on the work item, it steers that agent. Otherwise it is added to the conversation for the next agent run. |

Approve, reject and answer only count when you are one of the gate's assignees, or the gate has none. Kiln matches your Slack user to a person through the server's `identities` map, for example `slack:U024BE7LH` to `po@acme.test`. Without a mapping, your Slack user ID must itself be an assignee. Replies that cannot decide the gate are handled like other text. See [Who may decide from a reply](../configuration/automations.md#who-may-decide-from-a-reply).

Decisions from Slack are recorded with your person (or Slack user ID) and `slack` as the surface, exactly like decisions from the web.

Steering from the thread works like steering from the run page. See [Harnesses](../infrastructure/harnesses.md#steering).

## Related pages

- [Automations](../configuration/automations.md)
- [Approving specs and previews](../product-owners/approving-specs-and-previews.md)
- [Inbox](../management/inbox.md)
- [How Kiln works](../overview/how-kiln-works.md)

# Admin, RBAC and audit

Source: https://github.com/fishuke/klin/blob/main/docs/site/management/admin-rbac-audit.md

Access to Kiln's API and MCP is controlled by tokens whose scopes are granted per factory, and every change people or Kiln make is written to the audit log.

## Tokens

A token belongs to a subject (a person or a service), has a name, a list of grants and an optional lifetime in hours. Kiln shows the token once, when it is issued, and stores only its hash. Tokens can be revoked; a revoked or expired token is refused.

Send it as `Authorization: Bearer <token>` to the API, and configure it in your MCP client for the Kiln MCP. See the [API overview](../developer-tools/api.md) and the [MCP reference](../developer-tools/mcp.md).

Only tokens with `admin` on `*` (or team owners and admins) can issue scoped tokens, list them, manage server secrets and read the audit log.

### Token types

| Type | Grants |
| --- | --- |
| `scoped` | The explicit grants it was issued with (`POST /api/v1/tokens`). The bootstrap admin token is one. |
| `session` | A login. Grants come from the user's team and factory roles, computed on every request. |
| `personal` | An API key that acts as its user, like a session. |
| `agent` | A team service account: `read` and `send` on the team's factories. |
| `worker` | A self-hosted worker. It has no API scopes. |

Sessions and personal, agent and worker keys are covered in [Teams and users](teams-and-users.md).

## Scopes

Each grant pairs one scope with one factory ID, or `*` for all factories.

| Scope | Allows |
| --- | --- |
| `read` | See factories, definitions, work items, runs, gates, scores, metrics, self-improvement proposals, benchmarks and memories. |
| `send` | Send work items, post messages, cancel work, pull a task to a local worktree and hand it back, steer, replay, pause, resume and cancel runs, propose memories, and create and plan projects. |
| `decide:spec` | Approve or reject spec gates. |
| `decide:preview` | Approve or reject preview gates. |
| `decide:question` | Answer, approve or reject question gates. |
| `decide:merge` | Decide merge and custom gates, and confirm a handed-off work item complete without a merge. |
| `definitions:write` | Apply, sync and connect definitions, promote or roll back canaries, run self-improvement and benchmarks, approve or reject proposals, accept or reject memories, save benchmark tasks, publish and install skills. |
| `admin` | Everything above on the granted factories, plus tokens, secrets and the audit log when granted on `*`. |

Rules:

- `admin` implies every other scope.
- There are no wildcard scopes such as `decide:*`. Grant each one you need.
- A grant for one factory never covers another. Only `*` covers all.
- Connecting a new config repo needs `definitions:write` on `*`, because the factory does not exist yet.

### Grant strings

Grants can be written as a comma-separated string of `<scope>:<factory>`:

```text
read:*,send:webapp,decide:spec:webapp,decide:preview:webapp
```

An unknown scope is an error.

### Typical tokens

| Who | Grants |
| --- | --- |
| Product owner | `read:*`, `send:<factory>`, `decide:spec:<factory>`, `decide:preview:<factory>`, `decide:question:<factory>` |
| Engineer | `read:*`, `send:<factory>`, `decide:question:<factory>`, `decide:merge:<factory>` |
| Factory engineer | `read:*`, `send:<factory>`, `definitions:write:<factory>` |
| CI validating definitions | Any valid token; validation needs no scope. Add `definitions:write:<factory>` to apply. |
| Admin | `admin:*` |

A product owner's token cannot touch definitions, and a `decide:preview` token cannot apply definition changes.

### Roles map onto scopes

People do not need hand-made grants. Their factory role (User, Editor or Admin) gives them the scopes in [Factory roles](teams-and-users.md#factory-roles), and team owners and admins are Admin on every factory in their team. A team-wide check (`*`), or a factory that does not exist yet, is decided by the team role. Members may `read` and `send`. Owners and admins may do everything.

## Run tokens are different

Agents never get API tokens. Each run gets its own run token, valid for 60 minutes, that can only push `kiln/*` branches of the run's repositories, open pull requests, comment and add labels. It can never approve or merge. See [Architecture and security](../infrastructure/architecture-and-security.md).

## Secrets

Admins store named secrets, such as webhook secrets and API keys, in Kiln. Listing secrets returns names only; values never leave the server through the API. When a secret is not in the store, Kiln looks for the server environment variable `KILN_SECRET_<NAME>`. The only plain environment variables Kiln reads as secrets are model-provider keys: `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN`, `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, `OPENAI_API_KEY`, `CODEX_API_KEY`, `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` and `GOOGLE_GENERATIVE_AI_API_KEY`. This way an agent definition cannot ask for the server's own credentials by name. Listing secrets includes names found in the environment.

These server secrets are the last place Kiln looks. Typed team and personal secrets, which most teams should use, are described in [Secrets, MCP servers and environments](secrets-mcps-environments.md).

## Audit log

Kiln writes an entry with the time, the actor, the action and the target for:

| Area | Actions |
| --- | --- |
| Definitions | `definition.applied` (with SHA, diff and canary share), `definition.rejected` (with errors), `canary.promoted`, `canary.rolled_back` |
| Work items | `work_item.created`, `work_item.cancelled`, `notify.failed` |
| Gates | `gate.approve`, `gate.reject`, `gate.answer`, with the surface used |
| Runs | `run.steered` (with the message), `run.cancelled`, `run.paused`, `run.resumed` |
| Self-improvement | `proposal.opened`, `proposal.approved`, `proposal.force_approved`, `proposal.rejected`, `proposal.empty`, `proposal.invalid` |
| Accounts | `user.created`, `user.password_changed`, `user.email_changed`, `user.account_linked`, `user.account_unlinked`, `auth.login`, `auth.login_failed`, `auth.logout`, `api_key.created`, `api_key.revoked` |
| Teams | `team.created`, `team.updated`, `team.avatar_changed`, `team.settings_changed`, `team.member_added`, `team.member_role_changed`, `team.member_removed`, `team.invite_created`, `team.invite_resent`, `team.invite_revoked`, `team.invite_accepted` |
| Factory roles | `factory.team_assigned`, `factory.member_added`, `factory.member_role_changed`, `factory.member_removed` |
| Secrets, MCP servers and environments | `secret.created`, `secret.updated`, `secret.deleted`, `mcp.created`, `mcp.updated`, `mcp.deleted`, `environment.created`, `environment.updated`, `environment.deleted` |
| Skills, memories and routers | `skill.published`, `skill.installed`, `memory.accepted`, `memory.rejected`, `router.proposed` |
| Planning and benchmarks | `project.created`, `roadmap.created`, `benchmark.ran` |
| Scoring | `score.invalid_label` |
| Admin | `token.issued`, `secret.set` |

The audit log returns the newest entries first, 200 by default.

Typed decisions have their own log with inputs, answers, action, provider, fallback and latency. See [Typed decisions](../configuration/decisions.md#logs).

## Related pages

- [Teams and users](teams-and-users.md)
- [Secrets, MCP servers and environments](secrets-mcps-environments.md)
- [Architecture and security](../infrastructure/architecture-and-security.md)

- [Self-hosting](../infrastructure/self-hosting.md)

# Inbox

Source: https://github.com/fishuke/klin/blob/main/docs/site/management/inbox.md

The inbox lists every open gate assigned to you across all factories, most urgent first, so you can approve, reject or answer in one place.

## What appears in the inbox

Each item is an open gate:

| Kind | Example title | You can |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Spec | Approve the spec for "Team invites" | Approve or reject with feedback |
| Preview | Accept the preview of "Team invites" | Approve or reject with feedback |
| Question | verify keeps failing on "Fix the nav" | Answer, approve to resume, or reject to cancel |
| Command approval | Allow implement to run a risky command? | Approve to run it, reject to block it |
| Merge | Merge "Team invites" | Approve to confirm completion without a merge |
| Custom | Legal sign-off | Approve or reject |

Each item shows its work item (title, state, factory, pull request, preview URL and spec), the question or details, and evidence links such as the spec pull request, the preview and the videos.

You see gates assigned to you, plus gates with no assignee. Assignees come from the gate's `approvers`; see [Pipelines and gates](../configuration/pipelines-and-gates.md#gates).

## Order

The `inbox-urgency` decision gives each gate an urgency score when it opens. The inbox sorts by urgency, highest first, then by age, oldest first. If the decision is not available, questions get 0.7 and other gates 0.5.

## Deciding

The inbox, Slack and issue replies, the API and the Kiln MCP all call the same decision code. Each decision records:

- the decision (`approve`, `reject` or `answer`),
- your answer or feedback,
- who decided and through which surface (`web`, `slack`, `linear`, `jira`, `github`, `mcp`),
- when.

The decision is added to the work item's conversation and counted as a human touch, and the audit log gets an entry. Deciding a gate that is already closed changes nothing.

A reply in Slack or on an issue or pull request decides a gate only when its author is one of the gate's assignees, or the gate has none. See [Who may decide from a reply](../configuration/automations.md#who-may-decide-from-a-reply).

Only question gates take free-text answers. To decide through the inbox, the API or the MCP, your token needs the matching scope for the factory:

| Gate kind | Scope |
| --- | --- |
| Spec | `decide:spec` |
| Preview | `decide:preview` |
| Question | `decide:question` |
| Merge and custom | `decide:merge` |

## Reminders and expiry

Gates with a `nudge` time post a reminder in the source thread at that interval, naming who the gate waits on. Gates with an `expire` time park, approve or reject on their own when it passes. The built-in spec and preview gates nudge every 24 hours and park after 72 hours. The merge gate nudges every 48 hours.

A command approval waits up to 30 minutes, then expires and the command is blocked.

## From the command line and MCP

`kiln inbox` lists your open gates. The Kiln MCP has `list_inbox` and `decide_gate`. See the [CLI reference](../developer-tools/cli.md) and the [MCP reference](../developer-tools/mcp.md).

## Weekly digest

The digest groups open gates by person, oldest first, with each one's age in hours and a link to it in the inbox.

## Related pages

- [Approving specs and previews](../product-owners/approving-specs-and-previews.md)
- [Pipelines and gates](../configuration/pipelines-and-gates.md)
- [Typed decisions](../configuration/decisions.md)
- [Admin, RBAC and audit](admin-rbac-audit.md)

# Portfolio and projects

Source: https://github.com/fishuke/klin/blob/main/docs/site/management/portfolio.md

A project groups the factories that serve one product or goal, and the portfolio rolls up their work, cost and pending decisions across every project.

## Projects

A project has a name, an owner and a list of factories, for example "Customer portal" with `webapp`, `api` and `mobile`. Creating a project links each listed factory to it.

To create a project through the API, your token needs `send` on every factory in it. The creator becomes the owner.

A work item sent through the API can name a project.

Each project can hold one roadmap from the [plan agent](../product-owners/planning.md). Making a new plan replaces the project's current roadmap.

## The portfolio

For each project, the portfolio shows each factory's [metrics](../measure-and-improve/metrics.md) and these totals:

| Total | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| PRs opened | Work items with a pull request, across the project's factories |
| PRs merged | Work items completed by a merge |
| Cost | Run costs in USD |
| Active work items | Work items not yet complete, cancelled or failed |
| Pending decisions | Open gates in the project's factories |

Across all factories it also shows the number of factories, PRs merged, cost and active work items.

Metrics cover the last 30 days by default. You can pass another start date.

## Weekly digest

The digest tells each person which decisions are waiting on them, oldest first, with a link to each one. See [Inbox](inbox.md#weekly-digest).

## Related pages

- [Planning](../product-owners/planning.md)
- [Dashboard metrics](../measure-and-improve/metrics.md)
- [Inbox](inbox.md)
- [Admin, RBAC and audit](admin-rbac-audit.md)

# Secrets, MCP servers and environments

Source: https://github.com/fishuke/klin/blob/main/docs/site/management/secrets-mcps-environments.md

Secrets, MCP servers and environments belong to a team. Agents use them by name, and Kiln resolves them for each run.

## Secrets

A secret has a scope, a name, a type, an optional description, and who created and last changed it and when. Values are write-only: the API returns metadata, never values. A value can be at most 128 KiB.

| Scope | Who manages it | Which runs get it |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `team` | Team owners and admins | Runs of the team's factories, when the agent asks for it |
| `personal` | You | Only runs you triggered: work you sent, or work whose requester resolves to your account |

When both scopes have a secret with the same name, a run you triggered gets your personal one.

### Types

| Type | Value | Gives the run |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `raw` | a string | An environment variable named after the secret |
| `docker_registry` | `{ host, username, password }` | Nothing in the environment. It is a private image credential. |
| `aws_ecr` | `{ roleArn, region }` (team scope only) | Nothing in the environment. It is an image credential. |
| `anthropic_api_key` | a string | `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` |
| `claude_oauth_token` | a string from `claude setup-token` | `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` |
| `anthropic_bedrock_api_key` | a string, or `{ apiKey, region }` | `AWS_BEARER_TOKEN_BEDROCK`, `AWS_REGION`, `CLAUDE_CODE_USE_BEDROCK=1` |
| `anthropic_bedrock_access_key` | `{ accessKeyId, secretAccessKey, sessionToken?, region }` | `AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID`, `AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY`, `AWS_SESSION_TOKEN`, `AWS_REGION`, `CLAUDE_CODE_USE_BEDROCK=1` |
| `openai_api_key` | a string | `OPENAI_API_KEY` |
| `openrouter_api_key` | a string | `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` |
| `google_api_key` | a string | `GOOGLE_GENERATIVE_AI_API_KEY` |

Kiln checks each value against its type. Secret names use letters, digits and underscores.

Manage secrets with `GET /api/v1/managed-secrets`, `POST /api/v1/managed-secrets`, `PATCH /api/v1/managed-secrets/<scope>/<name>` (new value or description) and `DELETE /api/v1/managed-secrets/<scope>/<name>`.

### How runs get secrets

- **Agent secrets:** an agent's `secrets` list names the secrets its runs get. Typed secrets give their provider variables. Agents get no secrets they do not list.
- **Harness credentials:** with `harness.auth: { source: secret, secretName: X }`, a typed secret `X` gives its provider variables. A raw secret goes to the harness's usual variable. Without `harness.auth`, Kiln picks the first credential the harness can use, from typed secrets and the names in [Harnesses](../infrastructure/harnesses.md#credentials). Claude Code also accepts Bedrock credentials.
- **Lookup order** for a name: your personal secret (for runs you triggered), then the team secret, then the server's secrets (the older admin `PUT /api/v1/secrets/<name>` store, model-provider environment variables and `KILN_SECRET_<NAME>`).
- **Redaction:** Kiln replaces every secret value a run could see with `[redacted]` in its events, tool output and summary.
- **Encryption:** with `KILN_SECRET_KEY` set, values are sealed with AES-256-GCM in the store. Without it they are stored in plain text, so set it on any shared server.

### Team-managed model keys

Team owners and admins set one key per provider with `PUT /api/v1/teams/<team>/model-keys/<provider>`:

| Provider | Team secret | Type |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `anthropic` | `KILN_MODEL_ANTHROPIC` | `anthropic_api_key` |
| `openai` | `KILN_MODEL_OPENAI` | `openai_api_key` |
| `openrouter` | `KILN_MODEL_OPENROUTER` | `openrouter_api_key` |
| `bedrock` | `KILN_MODEL_BEDROCK` | `anthropic_bedrock_access_key`, or `anthropic_bedrock_api_key` when you send an API key |

Runs without their own harness credential use these. `GET /api/v1/teams/<team>/model-keys` shows which keys are set.

## MCP servers ("MCPs and apps")

Team owners and admins register MCP servers for the team. Agents name them in `mcpServers`, by name or id.

```json
{ "name": "figma", "url": "https://mcp.figma.com/mcp", "headers": { "Authorization": "Bearer {{FIGMA_TOKEN}}" } }
{ "name": "sentry", "command": "npx", "args": ["-y", "@sentry/mcp-server"], "env": { "SENTRY_TOKEN": "{{SENTRY_TOKEN}}" }, "mode": "direct" }
```

- A server has either `command` with `args` and `env`, or `url` with `headers`.
- `{{NAME}}` refers to a secret, looked up the same way as agent secrets.
- **Connection mode `managed`** (the default for URL servers): Kiln puts the secret values into the harness's MCP config.
- **Connection mode `direct`** (the default for command servers): the config keeps `${NAME}` references, and the values go into the run's environment. Values are never written to disk.
- A server whose secrets are missing, or a name Kiln does not know, is skipped. The run shows an `mcp_skipped` event.

### Built-in integration servers

These servers can be referenced by id without registering them. They are listed as connected once their secrets exist in the team or on the server.

| `kiln_id` | Server | Needs |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `linear` | Linear's hosted MCP | `LINEAR_API_KEY` |
| `slack` | `@modelcontextprotocol/server-slack` | `SLACK_BOT_TOKEN` |
| `jira` | `mcp-atlassian` | `JIRA_BASE_URL`, `JIRA_EMAIL`, `JIRA_API_TOKEN` |
| `github` | GitHub's hosted MCP | `GITHUB_MCP_TOKEN` (use a read-mostly token; agents never get merge rights) |
| `discord` | `mcp-discord` | `DISCORD_BOT_TOKEN` |

Every run also gets the Kiln MCP server with its own run token.

## Environments

An environment is a team template: a Docker image, repositories, setup commands and secrets. Point a factory at one with `environmentId` in `agentDefaults`, an agent or an automation. You can use the id or the name. The most specific setting wins.

```yaml
# factory.yaml
agentDefaults:
  harness: { type: claude-code }
  environmentId: node-24
```

At run time:

- The image is used when the agent names no runner.
- The environment's repositories are cloned next to the factory's.
- Its setup commands run after the runner's setup commands.
- Its secrets are added to the agent's secrets.
- An `environmentId` that the team does not have stops the run with a clear error.

Manage environments with `GET`, `POST`, `PATCH` and `DELETE /api/v1/environments`.

## Related pages

- [Teams and users](teams-and-users.md)
- [Harnesses](../infrastructure/harnesses.md)
- [Agents](../configuration/agents.md)
- [Admin, RBAC and audit](admin-rbac-audit.md)

---

# Teams and users

Source: https://github.com/fishuke/klin/blob/main/docs/site/management/teams-and-users.md

People sign in to Kiln with an account, work in one or more teams, and get a role on each factory. Every API request acts as a user, a team service account or a scoped token.

## Accounts and login

An account has a name, an email, an optional avatar and a password (stored as a salted scrypt hash) or a linked GitHub login.

- **Sign up:** `POST /api/v1/auth/signup` with `email`, `password` (at least 8 characters) and optionally `name` and `invite`.
- **Log in:** `POST /api/v1/auth/login` returns a session token. Send it as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`. Sessions last 30 days.
- **Log out:** `POST /api/v1/auth/logout` revokes the session token.
- **GitHub login:** set `GITHUB_CLIENT_ID` and `GITHUB_CLIENT_SECRET` on the server, and use `<public URL>/api/v1/auth/github/callback` as the OAuth app's callback URL. `GET /api/v1/auth/github/start?redirect=<web URL>` sends people to GitHub. They come back to the web app with the session token in the URL fragment. Kiln finds the account by the linked GitHub id, then by verified email. If neither matches, it signs the person up under the rules below.

`GET /api/v1/auth/providers` tells a login page which methods are on and whether signup is open.

### Who may sign up

1. The first person to sign up becomes the owner of the default team.
2. After that, signing up needs an invite for the same email address.
3. With `KILN_OPEN_SIGNUP=1`, anyone may sign up and joins the default team as a member.

### Local development

With `KILN_DEV_AUTH=1`, requests without a token act as the seeded user `dev@kiln.local`. That user owns the default team and has `admin` on every factory. Requests that do send a token still act as that token, so you can try logins locally. Never turn dev auth on for a server others can reach.

The bootstrap admin token that the server prints on first start keeps working. It is a scoped token with `admin` on every factory, not a user.

## Teams

A team has a name, a slug, an avatar and settings. Each factory belongs to one team. Factories created before teams existed move into the default team on start.

| Team role | Can |
| --- | --- |
| `owner` | Everything an admin can, plus grant or take away ownership. A team always keeps at least one owner. |
| `admin` | Rename the team, manage members, invites, settings, team secrets, MCP servers, environments and model keys, and create agent and worker keys. Admin on every factory in the team. |
| `member` | Use the team's factories with the team's default factory role, add personal secrets, create personal API keys. |

Anyone with an account can create a team (`POST /api/v1/teams`) and becomes its owner.

### Current team

Requests act in one team at a time. Send `X-Kiln-Team: <team id or slug>` to choose it. Without the header, Kiln uses your first team. Factory lists, secrets, MCP servers, environments and usage show the current team only. Agent and worker keys always act in their own team.

The SDK sets the header with `client.withTeam("payments")`.

### Invites

Owners and admins invite people by email with a role (`POST /api/v1/teams/<team>/invites`). The response holds the invite link, `<web URL>/join?invite=<token>`. Kiln stores only a hash of the token.

- An invite expires after 7 days.
- **Resend** issues a new link and 7 more days. The old link stops working.
- **Revoke** cancels the invite.
- `GET /api/v1/invites/<token>` shows the team, email and role without logging in.
- People with an account accept with `POST /api/v1/invites/accept`. New people sign up with the `invite` field.
- Only owners can invite owners.

### Team settings

| Setting | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `spendLimit.monthlyUsd` | `200` | The monthly spend limit. See [Usage and spend limits](usage-and-spend-limits.md). |
| `spendLimit.autoStop` | `false` | Refuse new runs once the limit is reached. When off, the limit is a soft warning. |
| `githubOrgs` | `[]` | Enabled GitHub orgs. When the list is not empty, the team's factories may only use GitHub repositories owned by these orgs. |
| `defaultSandboxHost` | not set | `local`, `docker` or `kubernetes`. Used for runs whose agent names no runner. |
| `egressAllowlist` | `[]` | Hosts added to every run's egress allowlist. |
| `storage.artifacts`, `storage.transcripts`, `storage.attachments` | `{ kind: local }` | Where each kind of data should go: a local folder (`path`) or an S3-compatible bucket (`bucket`, `region`, optional `endpoint`, `prefix`, `forcePathStyle`, and the names of team secrets holding the access key). |
| `defaultFactoryRole` | `user` | The factory role every member has on the team's factories: `none`, `user` or `editor`. |

Kiln validates and stores the `storage` settings, but files are still written to the server's object store (`KILN_DATA_DIR/objects`). Writing to a team's own bucket is not built yet.

Team-managed model keys (Anthropic, OpenAI, OpenRouter, Bedrock) are team secrets with fixed names. See [Secrets, MCP servers and environments](secrets-mcps-environments.md#team-managed-model-keys).

## Factory roles

| Factory role | Can | Scopes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| User | See the factory, send work, decide spec, preview and question gates, propose memories. | `read`, `send`, `decide:spec`, `decide:preview`, `decide:question` |
| Editor | Everything a User can, plus edit the definition, agents, repos and automations, attach secrets, MCP servers and runners, and confirm merges. | adds `definitions:write`, `decide:merge` |
| Admin | Everything, including factory members and forcing a definition change that waits for a second approval (`POST /api/v1/proposals/<id>/approve` with `{ "force": true }`). | `admin` |

Team owners and admins are always Admin. Members get the team's `defaultFactoryRole`, or a higher role from a factory membership. Manage factory memberships with `GET`, `POST`, `PATCH` and `DELETE /api/v1/factories/<id>/members`. The person must be in the factory's team first.

Kiln turns roles into the same per-factory scopes that tokens use, when each request arrives. Every route checks scopes the same way for users and tokens. See [Admin, RBAC and audit](admin-rbac-audit.md).

Team-wide actions, and applying a definition for a factory that does not exist yet, are decided by the team role. Members may read and send. Owners and admins may do everything.

## API keys

Create keys in user settings (`POST /api/v1/api-keys`). Keys use the `kiln_` format and are shown once.

| Type | Acts as | Who creates it |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `personal` | You, with your roles. Usage counts as yours. | Anyone |
| `agent` | A team service account: `read` and `send` on the team's factories, never decide or merge. Usage counts as the team's. | Team owners and admins |
| `worker` | A self-hosted worker. It has no API scopes. | Team owners and admins |

Expiry is `1d`, `30d` (the default), `90d` or `never`. The key list shows when each key was last used. Revoke a key with `DELETE /api/v1/api-keys/<id>`. Team owners and admins also see and revoke the team's agent and worker keys.

## User settings

`PATCH /api/v1/me` changes:

- `name` and `email`.
- `avatar`: a URL, or `null` to clear it. You can also upload an image with `PUT /api/v1/me/avatar` (PNG, JPEG, GIF, WebP or SVG, at most 1 MiB).
- `appearance`: `light`, `dark` or `system`.
- `notifications`: for each inbox kind (`spec`, `preview`, `question`, `merge`, `custom`), whether to notify by `email`, `slack` and `discord`.

Change your password with `PUT /api/v1/me/password`.

`GET /api/v1/me` returns your user, your teams, the current team, your role in it, your role on each factory, and the token's grants.

### Linked accounts

Linked accounts tell Kiln who you are on other systems. Supported providers: `github`, `slack`, `discord`, `linear`, `jira`, `teams`, `gitlab` and `azure_devops`.

- Link one with `POST /api/v1/me/linked-accounts` and `{ "provider": "slack", "externalId": "U024BE7LH" }`. Add `handle` for a login name such as a GitHub username.
- Unlink with `DELETE /api/v1/me/linked-accounts/<provider>`.
- One external account belongs to one user.

When an event arrives, for example a Slack reply in a work item's thread, Kiln looks up the author:

1. A linked account.
2. The server's `identities` option.
3. An email that matches an account. Linear and Jira send emails.

The result becomes the work item's requester and the person who decides a gate from a reply. GitHub login links your GitHub account automatically.

## Related pages

- [Admin, RBAC and audit](admin-rbac-audit.md)
- [Secrets, MCP servers and environments](secrets-mcps-environments.md)
- [Usage and spend limits](usage-and-spend-limits.md)
- [API reference](../developer-tools/api.md)
- [Self-hosting](../infrastructure/self-hosting.md)
